First, I collected these, primitively equipped as I was. Driven by curiosity, I ventured north into what appeared to be a store. There, I added to my inventory, retrieving the coil of rope, before pausing to examine the kettle.

I found myself on a small, dimly lit ship, confined to the cramped galley. The air was thick with salt and the scent of paraffin, a stark reminder of the sea's endless presence. My hands, rough from constant contact with rough timber and salt-encrusted metal, had managed to pick up a kettle from the floor. It was a seemingly insignificant object, but its existence in this isolated space was curious.

Venturing further north, I found myself in an abandoned store, its shelves sparse, echoing with a haunting emptiness. It was here I collected another item - a coil of rope. Its presence felt out of place amidst the paraffin fumes, hinting at a variety of past uses. Intrigued, I decided to move upwards, climbing the stairs to explore the vessel's unknown upper regions.

I also discovered a logbook in the workshop but was unable to read it. Despite the gantry leading to different parts of the ship, I was unable to venture beyond certain boundaries. My journey here has been one of exploration and discovery, with every turn revealing more about this submerged world.
